added.title: Software Dev Engineer, AWS Agentic AI Dev Ops
added.description:
Description

Do you want to build the next generation of Agentic AI developer and operations tools?

We are the AWS DevOps Agent UI + Remote Servers team under the Agentic AI DevOps organization. We own the client-facing surface of the AWS DevOps Agent: the web applications customers work in every day, the authentication layer that secures every session, the RBAC system that governs what each user and agent can do, and the Remote Servers that connect the agent to customer environments. These are the interfaces and access controls through which customers experience Agentic Chat — an AI teammate that understands context across investigations, delivers real-time insights, and helps prevent incidents before they occur.

As a Software Development Engineer on our team, you'll work across the entire stack — from responsive, high-performance front-end web applications to the auth, authorization, and server-side systems that make them secure and reliable at scale. You'll build customer-facing experiences on top of Large Language Models and agentic backends, design and harden authentication and RBAC flows, and extend the Remote Server layer that bridges the agent to real infrastructure. You'll partner closely with backend, science, and product teams, ship rapid prototypes, and take challenging, broadly defined problems from idea to production.

We are looking for a talented, versatile Software Development Engineer who thrives on working across the stack in a fast-paced environment. You should bring a strong technical background, customer obsession, and a bias for action, with a proven track record of delivering robust solutions quickly. Strong judgment and communication skills, long-term technical vision, and a relentless focus on engineering, security, and operational excellence are essential. You'll demonstrate technical proficiency, mentor and grow junior engineers, champion software development best practices, and iterate quickly to deliver results.

We foster a collaborative environment where innovation thrives and technical excellence is the standard. Every team member has the opportunity to shape the future of AI-powered DevOps while maintaining work-life balance and pursuing continuous learning.

Key job responsibilities

Design and build customer-facing web applications and interfaces that deliver meaningful customer impact in a large distributed computing environment.
Build and harden the authentication and RBAC systems that secure customer and agent access across the product.
Extend and operate the Remote Servers layer that connects the DevOps Agent to customer environments reliably and at scale.
Work across the full stack — front-end, APIs, auth, and server-side services — to deliver cohesive, end-to-end experiences.
Integrate LLM-powered and agentic capabilities into intuitive, performant user experiences, partnering with Applied Scientists and backend teams.
Work in an agile environment to deliver high-quality software quickly while maintaining engineering excellence.

A day in the life

Diverse Experiences

AWS values diverse experiences. Even if you do not meet all of the preferred qualifications and skills listed in the job description, we encourage candidates to apply. If your career is just starting, hasn’t followed a traditional path, or includes alternative experiences, don’t let it stop you from applying.

Why AWS?

Amazon Web Services (AWS) is the world’s most comprehensive and broadly adopted cloud platform. We pioneered cloud computing and never stopped innovating — that’s why customers from the most successful startups to Global 500 companies trust our robust suite of products and services to power their businesses.

Inclusive Team Culture

AWS values curiosity and connection. Our employee-led and company-sponsored affinity groups promote inclusion and empower our people to take pride in what makes us unique. Our inclusion events foster stronger, more collaborative teams. Our continual innovation is fueled by the bold ideas, fresh perspectives, and passionate voices our teams bring to everything we do.

Mentorship & Career Growth

We’re continuously raising our performance bar as we strive to become Earth’s Best Employer. That’s why you’ll find endless knowledge-sharing, mentorship and other career-advancing resources here to help you develop into a better-rounded professional.

Work/Life Balance

We value work-life harmony. Achieving success at work should never come at the expense of sacrifices at home, which is why we strive for flexibility as part of our working culture. When we feel supported in the workplace and at home, there’s nothing we can’t achieve.

About The Team

Application Topology Service team curate and maintains application topology of AWS applications.

Basic Qualifications

3+ years of non-internship professional software development experience
2+ years of non-internship design or architecture (design patterns, reliability and scaling) of new and existing systems experience
1+ years of software development engineer or related occupational experience
1+ years of designing and developing large-scale, multi-tiered, multi-threaded, embedded or distributed software applications, tools, systems, and services using: C#, C++, Java, or Perl experience
1+ years of Object Oriented Design experience
Bachelor's degree or foreign equivalent in Computer Science, Engineering, Mathematics, or a related field
Experience programming with at least one software programming language

Preferred Qualifications

3+ years of full software development life cycle, including coding standards, code reviews, source control management, build processes, testing, and operations experience
Bachelor's degree in computer science or equivalent

added.title: Member of Technical Staff, AI (Systems) Platform
added.description:
Beacon Holdings is acquiring and operating a portfolio of vertical SaaS companies. Most private equity firms scale by adding people. We are building Beacon to scale by adding software. The thesis is simple. Portfolio operations, value creation, and deal sourcing are bottlenecked by human attention, and the right software platform can lift that ceiling by an order of magnitude.

We are building that platform: an agentic operating system that our portfolio companies run on. It is a problem set with real data, real multi-tenant requirements, and very few precedents to copy from.

Beacon has raised $750M+ from investors including General Catalyst, Lightspeed, D1 Capital, CPMG, and the family offices of the founders of Stripe, DoorDash, and Ramp.

About The Role

Members of Technical Staff (MTS) build the platform that everything else at Beacon runs on. You will own a piece of it end-to-end: design, implementation, operations, and long-term technical direction. This is a Staff Engineer role in everything but name. We run flat.

We are hiring for two roles. The bar is the same; the specialty differs.

Product and platform engineering. A senior engineer who builds agentic products and the platform underneath them: services, APIs, data access, and deploy infrastructure. Works directly with the people who use them.
AI infrastructure. An engineer who builds the systems around models: serving, retrieval, evals, observability, fine-tuning, and deployment into secure and regulated environments.

Both seats ship to real businesses, fast. You take a problem from the first conversation with a user to a system in production, and measure success by whether people use it.

What You'll Do

You will own one or both of these areas end-to-end:
Agentic products. Build the AI-native tools that operators across our portfolio use every day. You own the full stack: agent loops, UI, internal APIs, and the deploy infrastructure other engineers build on. The bar is not demos. It is tools people choose to open on Monday morning.
AI infrastructure. Serve and operate models, including open-weight ones, across cloud, VPC, and isolated environments. Fine-tune open-weight models on proprietary data where a general model falls short. Build the retrieval and governed data access that ground agents in real business data. Choose which model handles which job, with cost, latency, and quality as explicit trade-offs.

Evals and observability. Build the harness that tells us whether the system is working: task-level evals from real workflows, traces and telemetry, replay, and regression suites that catch quality drops before users do. Use the same signals to speed up root-cause analysis when things break.
How you will work:
Ship to real businesses, fast. Take a problem from the first user conversation to a system in production.
Prove quality with data. No model or prompt change ships on vibes.
Work agent-first. Agents are part of how you build, not just what you build.

Who You Are

Deep systems engineering. 5+ years building and operating distributed systems that real businesses depend on: databases, data platforms, query engines, control planes, or large-scale services. You have profiled your way to a 10x win, and you know where things break: partial failure, capacity limits, multi-tenant isolation, schema and API evolution. You write clean code in at least one of Python, Java, Go, C++, Rust, or TypeScript.
LLMs in production, not in slides. You have shipped LLM or agentic systems that people rely on: RAG over real enterprise data, agentic workflows, LLM-assisted diagnosis or operations. Coding agents are part of your daily loop. You know how these systems fail: hallucinated tool calls, silent quality drift, cost blowups, evals that measure the wrong thing.
Close to the customer. You have been on customer calls, run escalations, and turned what you heard into a product. You measure success by adoption, not launch.
Built from zero, run in production. You have been a founding engineer or taken a system from 0-to-1 through GA. You have also carried the pager: incident command, postmortems, and the fixes that keep the same outage from happening twice.
Comfortable with ambiguity. The scope of the platform is still being defined. Decisions you make in week one will shape what is possible in year three. That should energize you.
For the product and platform seat: strong on backend services, APIs and client architecture, internal tools, and deploy infrastructure, with enough front-end range to ship a full product. You have built products where the agent is the core of the experience, not a chat box bolted on.
For the AI infrastructure seat: hands-on with model serving (vLLM, llama.cpp, or similar), retrieval and vector search, evals, fine-tuning, and model routing. You have deployed into environments you do not fully control, such as customer VPCs or regulated and isolated regions, and you reason about GPU memory, batching, and quantization as fluently as about API design.

Preferred Skills

Built on or inside modern data platforms: Iceberg, lakehouse architectures, Snowflake, Databricks, or data catalogs and governance.
Performance engineering at scale: profiling, capacity planning, and measurable cost reductions.
Shipped into regulated environments: FedRAMP, government or sovereign regions, or air-gapped deployments.
Built LLM-assisted observability or root-cause analysis over real production telemetry.
Operated open-weight inference in production: batching, KV cache, quantization, speculative decoding, multi-GPU serving.
Founding engineer, co-founder, or first-hire experience.
Prior Staff or Principal Engineer experience at a high-bar engineering org.
Open-source contributions to data infrastructure, inference, evals, or developer tooling.

Our Values at Beacon Holdings:

Humility: We acknowledge that the path to getting to the right answer involves being wrong along the way. We have strong beliefs which are weakly held. We actively seek new ideas and believe we can learn from anyone at any time.
Honesty: We are truth seeking in our approach to business problems. Business is a repeat game and we believe that human relationships generate alpha. We understand that trust is earned over a lifetime and can be lost in an instant.
Hunger: We play to win. We hold ourselves to high standards and will not be outworked. We take pride in having a deep sense of responsibility to ourselves, each other, our partners, and our customers. We believe to whom much is given much is expected.
Horizon: We seek to build a generational software company. This will take decades. We manage our expectations and those of our partners to take advantage of the 8th wonder of the world - compounding growth.

How We Use AI in Our Hiring Process:
To ensure transparency, we want candidates to know that Beacon Software uses Artificial Intelligence and AI-enabled tools to assist with screening, reviewing, organizing and highlighting profiles and applications that match the key requirements for each role.

AI does not make hiring decisions:
Every application is reviewed by a member of our team, and all decisions throughout the process are made by humans. We use AI to support efficiency and consistency, not to replace human judgment. We are committed to a fair, thoughtful, and equitable experience for every candidate.

Description

The Region Flexibility Engineering (RFE) team builds and leverages foundational infrastructure capabilities, tools, and datasets needed to support the rapid global expansion of Amazon's SOA infrastructure. Our team focuses on robust and scalable architecture patterns and engineering best practices, driving adoption of ever-evolving and AWS technologies. RFE is looking for a passionate, results-oriented, inventive Data Scientist to refine and execute experiments towards our grand vision, influence and implement technical solutions for regional placement automation, cross-region libraries, and tooling useful for teams across Amazon.

As a Data Scientist in Region Flexibility, you will work to enable Amazon businesses to leverage new AWS regions and improve the efficiency and scale of our business. Our project spans across all of Amazon Stores, Digital and Others (SDO) Businesses and we work closely with AWS teams to advise them on SDO requirements. As innovators who embrace new technology, you will be empowered to choose the right highly scalable and available technology to solve complex problems and will directly influence product design. The end-state architecture will enable services to break region coupling while retaining the ability to keep critical business functions within a region. This architecture will improve customer latency through local affinity to compute resources and reduce the blast radius in case of region failures. We leverage off the sciences of data, information processing, machine learning, and generative AI to improve user experience, automation, service resilience, and operational efficiency.

Key job responsibilities

As an RFE Data Scientist, you will work closely with product and technical leaders throughout Amazon and will be responsible for influencing technical decisions and building data-driven automation capabilities in areas of development/modeling that you identify as critical future region flexibility offerings. You will identify both enablers and blockers of adoption for region flex, and build models to raise the bar in terms of understanding questions related to data set and service relationships and predict the impact of region changes and provide offerings to mitigate that impact.

The Regional Flexibility Engineering (RFE) organization supports the rapid global expansion of Amazon's infrastructure. Our projects support Amazon businesses like Stores, Alexa, Kindle, and Prime Video. We drive adoption of ever-evolving and AWS and non-AWS technologies, and work closely with AWS teams to improve AWS public offerings. Our organization focuses on robust and scalable solutions, simple to use, and delivered with engineering best practices. We leverage and build foundational infrastructure capabilities, tools, and datasets that enable Amazon teams to delight our customers. With millions of people using Amazon’s products every day, we appreciate the importance of making our solutions “just work”.

added.description:
Why Harvey

At Harvey, we’re transforming how legal and professional services operate. By combining frontier agentic AI, an enterprise-grade platform, and deep domain expertise, we’re reshaping how critical knowledge work gets done for decades to come.

This is a rare chance to help build a generational company at a true inflection point. We have strong product-market fit and world-class investor support. We’re scaling fast and defining a new category in real time. The work is ambitious, the bar is high, and the opportunity for growth — personal, professional, and financial — is unmatched.

Our team moves fast, takes ownership, and is deeply committed to the mission — operating with intensity, staying close to our customers, and pushing each other for excellence. We live by three values: Decisiveness, Simplicity, and Job's Not Finished. We act quickly on clear judgment over perfect information, we believe simplicity is what scales, and we're never satisfied with where we are. If you want to do the best work of your career alongside people who share that drive, we'd love to build with you.

At Harvey, the future of professional services is being written today — and we’re just getting started.

Role Overview

Harvey's brand team has built a creative agent that makes on-brand work on request: ads, social posts, decks, product films, and tailored demo videos for prospects. It reads our brand guidelines and design system live, works in the same tools our designers use, and hands back files a designer can open and keep editing.

We're hiring a senior engineer to own it. You'll spend most of your time building the agent and some of it making real work with it, because shipping with it is the fastest way to find what's broken. You'll report to our Creative Director and work closely with the designers, marketers, and sales teams who use the agent every day.

By the end of your first year, account executives and marketers make the work they need, on brand, without waiting on a designer.

What You'll Do

Own the creative agent end to end: its skills, templates, tool connections, and the quality of what it makes
Turn how our designers work into reusable recipes, so a request for an ad or a demo video comes back as work a Creative Director would approve
Build and run the media pipelines behind our films and ads, including rendering, video and audio processing, voiceover, music, and generated imagery
Write evals that catch off-brand copy, layout, and numbers before anyone sees them
Make the agent dependable for people who aren't designers, with clear questions when something is missing and recovery when a tool fails
Ship creative work with the agent every week, and feed what you learn back into it
Decide with the Creative Director what to build next, based on how people use it

What You Have

A designer's eye. You notice when a layout, a line, or an edit is off, and you fix it. Show us through a portfolio, side projects, or tools you've built.
Experience running LLM agents in production: tool use, MCP, prompt and skill design, evals, and the failures that only show up with real users
Experience building media pipelines with tools like ffmpeg, rendering engines, or generative image and video models
Five or more years as a software engineer. You are comfortable with the traditional full stack tool chain. You build with agents every day now, and you still have the fundamentals to review their code, debug it, and design systems that hold up.
Clear writing, for engineers and designers alike

Nice to Have

Experience with the Figma Plugin API or building on other design tools
A background in design, motion, film, or advertising
Internal tools you've built that people outside engineering chose to use

added.title: Sr. Applied Scientist, AWS Applied AI Solutions - Life Sciences
added.description:
Description

AWS Applied AI Solutions (AAIS) is building toward a future where every business innovates with Amazon AI teammates. To get there, we build AI solutions that improve human capabilities and transform entire business functions. We create end-to-end products that surprise and delight out-of-the-box, making complex things easy and hard things possible, with no cloud experience required. We start with customers who embrace the future and build bridges to meet the rest where they are. We pursue ambitious opportunities with conviction, and we are looking for builders who share that mindset.

The Team Join the next science revolution at AWS Life Sciences Applied AI Solutions where you'll work alongside world-class scientists to build AI that transforms how therapeutics are discovered, developed, and brought to patients.

We're out to revolutionize how medicines are discovered, developed, and brought to patients powered by a new generation of AI. Our team tackles some of the hardest open problems at the intersection of frontier AI and life sciences. We apply biological foundation models large language models and agentic reasoning systems to life sciences problems then put them into the hands of customers as applications and managed services they can fine-tune tailor and deploy on their own data. The science challenges are deep: how do you design agentic systems that reason correctly over complex biological regulatory and clinical logic? How do you enable customers to tailor foundation models to their proprietary data and get better outputs with less effort? How do you adapt models to reason faithfully in high-stakes scientific and regulatory domains?

Today we're focused on two areas. In clinical trials we're building AI that automates and optimizes regulatory and clinical development workflows. In drug design our products (including Amazon Bio Discovery) accelerate discovery by giving bench scientists AI-guided protein engineering and antibody design capabilities. We combine frontier research with production-scale delivery to put breakthrough science into the hands of customers solving humanity's hardest problems.

We value scientific rigor encourage publication and support conference participation. If you want to do research that ships this is the team.

The Role We are seeking an Applied Scientist to build the models and methods behind our life sciences AI products with a primary focus on clinical trial operations and agentic reasoning. You will design train and evaluate systems that reason over complex clinical and operational logic and ship them into products customers use directly. You will work closely with senior and principal scientists on well-scoped research problems own your results end to end and see your work reach production.

Role

This role combines expertise in LLM reasoning and agentic AI with applied impact in life sciences. You will work on how large language models reason plan and act in complex scientific domains while applying domain knowledge to ensure models produce scientifically valid outputs. The problems span multiple fronts:

How do you build LLM-based agentic systems that correctly reason over clinical protocols regulatory standards and complex multi-step operational workflows?
How do you evaluate agent reliability and faithfulness rigorously enough to trust in high-stakes clinical settings?
How do you develop model customization methods (fine-tuning retrieval augmentation domain adaptation) that let customers get strong results from foundation models on their own data?

You will focus on clinical trial operations (agentic automation structured reasoning evaluation domain adaptation) with opportunities to contribute across drug discovery (protein engineering antibody design) as the portfolio grows. You will own end-to-end scientific solutions from research through production and your work will directly shape the tools that scientists use daily.

Key job responsibilities

Design train fine-tune and evaluate LLM-based agentic systems that reason over clinical protocols regulatory standards and operational workflows
Build rigorous evaluation harnesses and benchmarks to measure agent reliability faithfulness and failure modes in high-stakes domains
Develop model customization methods (fine-tuning RLHF retrieval augmentation domain adaptation) that help customers get better outputs on their own data with less effort
Contribute to graph-based and causal modeling approaches for clinical trial operations
Partner with Life Sciences domain experts product and engineering to translate scientific challenges into shipped capabilities
Own experiments end to end: problem framing implementation evaluation iteration and hand-off to production
Publish at top-tier venues where the work supports it
Contribute to drug discovery efforts (protein engineering antibody design) as opportunities arise

A day in the life

We act quickly on clear judgment over perfect information, we believe simplicity is what scales, and we're never satisfied with where we are. If you want to do the best work of your career alongside people who share that drive, we'd love to build with you.

At Harvey, the future of professional services is being written today — and we’re just getting started.

added.description:
Description

Amazon Ads is one of the fastest-growing advertising businesses in the world, connecting brands with hundreds of millions of customers across shopping, streaming, gaming, audio and the open web. Behind every ad that runs on Prime Video, Twitch, IMDb and thousands of external publisher apps and sites is a decisioning platform built by Amazon Ads Supply Tech.

That platform makes X trillion ad decisions every day and supports $XB+ in annual publisher revenue across XX+ Amazon-owned publishers and X,000+ external publishers in streaming TV, audio, display, mobile and podcasts. Every one of those decisions is a science problem: which inventory qualifies for which buyers, how publisher commitments are paced and delivered, which ad wins among competing candidates, and what price maximizes long-term yield. Each must be solved in milliseconds, under strict latency and cost budgets, while balancing advertisers, publishers, viewers and Amazon. At this scale, a fraction-of-a-percent model improvement is worth $X millions.

We are looking for a Principal Applied Scientist to set the science strategy for this platform. You will decide where machine learning creates the most value, bring intelligence into real-time runtime systems, and lead models from idea to production. Your work will directly shape three of Amazon Ads’ biggest priorities: growing Amazon-owned and third-party supply, enabling full-funnel advertising, and building agentic, AI-driven workflows for publishers and advertisers.

As a principal, you will be a technical leader across the organization. You will raise the science bar, mentor senior scientists, and influence product and engineering leaders. You will work alongside excellent, driven scientists, engineers and product leaders who take on hard problems and invest in each other’s growth. Few places in the world operate at this scale.

Key job responsibilities

Define the ML strategy for the ad decisioning platform. Set a multi-year science vision across pricing, yield optimization, forecasting, ad selection and commitment delivery, tied to measurable business outcomes.
Identify opportunities to deploy intelligence in runtime systems. Find where rules and heuristics in real-time serving paths can be replaced or improved by learned models, and partner with engineering to fit them within latency, compute and reliability budgets.
Build ML models that operate at X trillion decisions a day, drawing on approaches such as deep learning, reinforcement learning and bandits, causal inference, forecasting, and auction and mechanism design.
Evaluate ML models rigorously. Design offline, counterfactual and off-policy evaluations and online experiments. Define metrics that capture long-term value for advertisers, publishers and viewers, not just short-term lift.
Refine models for output quality and performance. Improve accuracy, calibration and robustness, cut serving latency and cost, and monitor models in production for drift and degradation.
Lead science across the organization. Set technical standards, review science designs and launches, and mentor and grow senior and principal-track scientists.
Push the frontier, including LLM and agentic approaches, and contribute to Amazon’s internal and external science community through papers, talks and patents.

A day in the life

Start the day reviewing off-policy evaluation results for a new pricing model that projects an X% yield lift, and deciding with your team whether it is ready for an online test. Next, you work with engineers on fitting a deeper model into a millisecond latency budget at X billion requests. At midday, you dig into why a forecasting model drifted during a live sports event, and sketch a fix. Later, you review a scientist’s paper draft and present the science roadmap to product leaders. Throughout, you work with brilliant, driven colleagues who sharpen your thinking and help you grow.

About The Team

Ads Decisioning team brings together applied scientists and product managers to build the intelligence behind Amazon’s publisher business. We serve Amazon-owned publishers such as Prime Video, Twitch and IMDb, along with thousands of external publishers across streaming TV, audio and display. Our models decide, in milliseconds, which inventory qualifies for which buyers, how commitments are delivered, which ad wins and at what price, balancing advertisers, publishers, viewers and Amazon. We pair scientific rigor with a bias for production impact, learn from each other, and invest in each other’s growth. Come solve problems few teams anywhere get to work on.

Basic Qualifications

5+ years of hands-on work in predictive modeling and analysis experience
PhD in Electrical Engineering, Computer Science, Mathematics, or a related technical field
Experience working in predictive modeling and analysis
Experience distilling informal customer requirements into problem definitions, dealing with ambiguity and competing objectives
Experience programming in Java, C++, Python or related language
Experience with leading experienced scientists as well as having a record of developing junior members from academia or industry to a career track in a business environment

Preferred Qualifications

10+ years of relevant work in industry or academia experience
Knowledge of problem solving, algorithm design and complexity analysis
Experience creating novel algorithms and advancing the state of the art
Have peer-reviewed scientific contributions in premier journals and conferences

added.title: Forward Deployed Strategist, New York
added.description:
Fifth Dimension is the most prominent AI company in real estate in the world, bringing the magic of AI automation to document-heavy industries 🌈. Our AI workspace helps leading investment managers, owners, and operators across the US, UK, and APAC automate complex workflows, extract insights from critical documents, and make faster, smarter decisions.

We're hiring a Forward Deployed Strategist to own delivery on our most important US accounts. You'll work in a pod with a forward deployed engineer, an account manager and our sales team, and you'll make the calls that decide whether a pilot becomes a firm-wide deployment: which workflow comes first, who needs to be in the room, what we build and what we don't. Customers will trust you because you understand their business. Our product team will listen to you because you've seen what works.

What a Week Looks Like

Monday.
Pod reviews across your three US accounts. One is on track. One has an MD asking for a bespoke dashboard. One has gone quiet: asset management hasn't logged in for ten days. You move that one to the top of the week.

Tuesday.
On site with the quiet account. You sit with two asset managers through quarter-end and find the step that eats a week a month: reconciling operator reports against the rent roll. By the afternoon you've built a first version in the product, on their own documents, and they've told you what it gets wrong.

Wednesday.
You move the FDE's week onto that workflow and off the dashboard. Then you write to the MD: why the dashboard can wait, what the team gets instead, and when.

Thursday.
Two hours with our CTO and the FDEs. Three accounts have asked for some version of the same reconciliation. You bring the brief: what's common, what's one customer's preference, and what the template should be.

Friday.
Three asset managers ran this week's reconciliation in 5D, and nobody opened the spreadsheet. You post the weekly update for each pod: what moved, what's stuck, what you decided. Then you sit in on a sales call with a prospect who has the same problem, to hear how they describe it.

This is a forward-deployed week at Fifth Dimension. You decide what we build for our most important customers, and you make sure they use it. What works in one account becomes product for all of them.

About Us

Fifth Dimension builds AI software for the firms that invest in and manage real assets. We help people work with complex documents and business data, from leases and financial models to investment memos. We're a Series A company with offices in London, New York and Singapore.

Our values are Own It, Ship It and Don't Be Boring. We move quickly, challenge each other kindly and care about making something customers actually use.

What This Role Is

Owning delivery at a strategic level on a few of our US enterprise accounts after they sign: the use cases, the plan, the narrative and the decisions.
Customer-facing for most of the week, often on site with investment, asset management and finance teams.
Directing forward-deployed engineering time: deciding what our FDEs build and why, and changing course when a rollout stalls.
The bridge to product: turning what works in one account into templates, skills and workflows that work in every account.
AI-first. You build with AI yourself, and you can tell a customer exactly where it will and won't help.

What This Role Is Not

A product manager role with a roadmap. You shape the product from the field; you don't own the backlog.
An engineering role. You don't need to write production code; our FDEs do. You do need to build in the product and understand what's being built.
Account management or customer success. Your pod has an account manager. You own the strategy, not the calendar.
Sales. There's no quota. You'll sit in on sales calls to learn the market, not to close.

The Challenge

A signed pilot is a bet, not a deployment. Real estate investment firms carry decades of process, documents in every format, and teams with good reason to be sceptical of AI. The first use case decides whether the rest of the firm follows.

Get it right and, six weeks in, the team uses it every day, the expansion conversation has started, and the workflow is a template every new customer starts from. Get it wrong and the pilot quietly expires.

What You'll Do

Own the delivery plan for each of your accounts: the use cases, their order, the success criteria agreed up front, and the evidence that they were met.
Decide where forward-deployed engineering time goes, and change it when a rollout stalls.
Build alongside the team: workspaces, skills and templates in the product, prototyped with AI.
Set the narrative: how the account understands 5D, from the analyst to the MD, including the hard conversations when expectations drift.
Bring the field back: a short weekly update per account, and briefs that turn repeatable work into product.
Become the domain expert in the room on the customer's workflow, their data and their language.

About You

You know real assets from the inside. You've worked in or alongside real estate investment, asset management or lending, and when you talk to a portfolio manager about a rent roll or an IC memo, they hear a peer. You've also lived with software: you've taken a product from signed to used, from either side of the table, and changed what it became with what you learned.

You're genuinely AI-native. You build with AI tools every week, whether workflows, analyses or prototypes, and you can say where it gets real estate wrong. You make decisions under ambiguity, hold your ground with senior people without losing them, and write clearly.

You might be inside an investment manager today, leading data or AI adoption, and want to do it for many firms instead of one. You might have been a deployment strategist, solutions lead or product person at a data or AI company and want to go deep in one industry. What you haven't done is spend a career in slide decks.

What We're Looking For

Real estate or real-assets experience, earned in investment, asset management, lending or a closely adjacent role. (Must-have.)
Software taken from contract to everyday use, ideally AI or data products, with what you learned fed back into the product. (Must-have.)
Hands-on AI in your own work: building, not just using. (Must-have.)
You've made the call when a rollout stalled: changed the use case, the plan or the people.
At ease with senior stakeholders, with examples of hard conversations you led.
A clear writer, for engineers and for executives.

Nice to Have

SQL or Python, or experience building on a data platform.
A forward-deployed, deployment-strategist or solutions role at an AI or data company.
Data modelling across asset classes and fund structures.
Product management experience at a B2B software company.

Your First Few Months

Month 1.
You've joined two live pods, met the decision-makers on both sides, and made your first delivery call. You've built your first workspace or skill with an FDE, and you can explain the product and its limits to an MD.

Month 3.
You run delivery strategy for your pods without escalating to the founders. At least one pilot is heading for expansion with evidence behind it, and something you built in the field is now a template in the product.

Month 6.
Your accounts are growing from pilot to full deployment. Several workflows that started in your pods ship as product, and new customers start from them.

Compensation And Benefits

We're hybrid: three days a week in our New York office, and on site with customers whenever their accounts need it.

$180,000–$250,000 base, plus meaningful equity. Flexible based on experience
Meaningful equity on a standard vesting schedule 📈
401(k) plan
Generous paid time off
Health, dental, and life insurance
Enhanced parental leave: 14 weeks for the primary caregiver, 6 weeks for the secondary caregiver
2-week all-company December shutdown

Process

A 30-minute call with our CTO, then a conversation with our co-founder and CPO. A case study built in the product, followed up with our CPO and one of our forward deployed engineers. Then time with the team you'd work with, and a final conversation with our CEO.

One More Thing

When you apply, send one example of a rollout you changed course on (anonymised), and one thing you built with AI that someone else used. A short description is fine.
